title: The Future of AI Software Factories- OpenCLAW, Agent Orchestration & The Intelligence Age with Mark Smith [MVP]
description:
What happens when AI agents become the whole software team? Mirko Peters talks with Mark Smith (NZ365Guy) about his OpenClaw-based AI software factory, Ralph loops, governance and why context engineering matters more than prompts. A practical look ahead for developers, consultants and IT leaders preparing for AI-first software engineering.
In this episode
00:00 – Welcome and introducing Mark Smith01:44 – From IT training to Dynamics CRM and Power Platform08:45 – Low code superseded by AI13:44 – Microsoft's AI strategy and Copilot adoption21:31 – Building a nine-agent AI software factory41:10 – OpenClaw, harnesses and Copilot Studio44:08 – Governance, email agents and AI at the edge50:19 – Preparing for an AI-first career and rapid fire
Key takeaways
Mark Smith runs a nine-agent AI software factory in which each agent fills one gated role in the DevOps loop, from requirements and architecture to coding, security, release and documentation.Owning the agent harness with OpenClaw keeps context and data in his own Azure environment, so models from different providers can be swapped without rebuilding the system.For an AI-first career, Mark recommends moving from prompt engineering to context and outcomes engineering, learning about harnesses and avoiding lock-in to a single vendor.
Worth quoting
“The day of low code has been superseded by AI. And that, I can do a lot more with a lot deeper technical functionality and technical ability.” – Mark Smith (08:45)
“And so what I loved about open claw is that I own the harness, right? I can plug, as I said, I've got nine different API connections, not even including open router.” – Mark Smith (41:10)
